title: Finding harmony through actual wishes

captions.physics: Coordinating different paces of an outing
captions.energy: Following vague expectations of the other
captions.emotions: Feeling different moods can be combined

meaning: Shared leisure gains living harmony when assumptions about another’s mood yield to voiced wishes and free coordination by both.
text: Different moods can meet without being guessed beforehand. Temperance in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps coordinate the paces of a pleasant outing. The Moon in energy leans towards vague expectations of the other person. Temperance in emotions allows harmony to feel possible. Her repeated appearance distinguishes action from experience. Genuine coordination needs actual preferences, beyond carefully adjusting to a version of how the other ought to enjoy today or the response they supposedly must receive.

Suppose you walk from a station to a small lake. One wants quiet observation, the other imagines conversation, but each assumes silence is the other’s preference. **Shared harmony grows from differences given words.** Discussing rhythm leaves room for a quiet stop and conversation. The walk takes your actual form. Identical feelings throughout are unnecessary, while a changed wish can be named without justifying the entire original idea or its promised picture of leisure.

The difficulty is mistaking anxious adjustment for harmony. You guess, accept something unspoken and become less certain that pleasure was shared. A calm appearance offers no clear answer. Temperance helps when combining what is heard. One concrete request can restore more warmth than lengthy balancing of imagined moods, preserving freedom to refine continuation without making each pause, smile or changed pace a hidden measure of correct shared feelings.
